function.description: Send a GET request to retrieve specified information for an interface from a network telemetry API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL endpoint to send the GET request to. This should include the base path without query parameters, e.g., 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'.

params.description: The query parameters for the request.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit nodes pertaining to.

nodeId.description: The node identifier to limit results pertaining to.

podId.description: The pod identifier to limit results pertaining to.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit results pertaining to.

infoType.description: The type of information requested for the interface.

message.content:
Below is the exact REST‑style GET request you would send to the Cisco Nexus Dashboard API to fetch the **Speed** information for the Ethernet interface on node 12 in pod 10 of fabric “Network1”.

```
GET https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo
    ?fabricName=Network1
    &nodeId=12
    &podId=10
    &interfaceType=Ethernet
    &infoType=Speed
```

### How to use it

| Tool | Example |
|------|---------|
| **curl** | `curl -k -X GET "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=Ethernet&infoType=Speed"` |
| **Postman** | Create a new GET request, paste the full URL above into the address bar, add any required authentication (e.g., Bearer token) in the Headers tab, then click *Send*. |

> **Note:**  
> * Replace `192.120.45.67` with your actual Nexus Dashboard IP if different.  
> * If the API requires authentication, add the appropriate header (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`).  
> * The `-k` flag in curl skips certificate verification – remove it if you’re using a trusted cert.

That’s all you need to generate the request.
